scope: 30_modules.md:Facts several modules touch, and their one owner

topics.topic: Ownership and enforcement of the canonical operation catalogue and owner-invocable operation set
questions: Which module owns the canonical identities and complete set of operations, including their surface, so that `operations`, `release_declarations`/`service_access`, and `owner_interface` cannot define different operation sets or names?

Which module owns the authoritative set of operations the owner may invoke, and which module enforces it at stage (1)? The changed text explains service authorization through `service_access` but leaves owner-operation authorization between `operations` and `owner_interface`, whose stated responsibilities point in opposite directions.

quotes:
The operation table: every operation of either surface with its stages and
the modules it changes — not which service may call it, which is the
release's table alone (A09 rule 2), asked of `service_access.service_may_call`
at stage (1); the owner's operations are the owner interface's.
Any check the server makes: the forms carry values, `operations` decides.
judgement.why: The texts do not make the proposed history admissible because no passage says an owner-interface request may name or dispatch an operation that is not an owner action, so the crafted request cannot supply a witness from the texts.

topics.topic: Ownership of service-to-operation permissions and highest disclosure-class facts
questions: Who owns the service-to-operations and highest-class facts: `release_declarations`, or `service_access`? If `service_access` owns only authentication and the decision returned by `service_may_call`, the text must distinguish that mechanism from ownership of the table.

topics.topic: Placement and transactional consequences of the disclosure-class check
questions: Is the disclosure-class refusal a stage-(1) authorization check performed before record processing, or a separate check after stages (3)–(6); if it is later, must a state-changing transaction be rolled back when it fails?
